title: fix(plugins): avoid shared capture collisions during setup
body:
Fixes #181423. Thanks @obviyus for the clean-install report and filesystem trace.

## What Problem This Solves

Fresh OpenAI setup can fail before its first provider request because plugin capture attempts to copy a shared file into a destination it already populated with a host-module symlink.

## User Impact

Shared import/asset references no longer cause `FsSafeError: creation target already exists`. Native Workers retain access to canonical host modules through capture recovery and disposal. No configuration, dependency, schema, or migration changes.

**Full packaged activation is not yet proven successful:** the smoke test reaches the local provider, then encounters further capture/packaging blockers described below.

## Why This Change Was Made

The overlap was introduced by [80778e082de5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/80778e082de5b30c079b5d7e6f38a2f0c3fd9fd3) (#181128). Shared imports create host links without entering copied-source bookkeeping; later asset capture reaches the exclusive file creator at the same destination.

The existing capture owner now records host-link destinations separately from copied plugin sources. Selective capture and recursive copying both preserve those destinations, including links retained during recovery. Denied file links still permit ordinary asset capture. Exclusive creation and host/SDK identity remain intact.

The regression extends the existing real Worker/recovery fixture with an import and an asset read of the same shared file. Production delta: +12/-1 lines; tests: +9/-1. The simplification pass retained one destination set shared by the two capture paths, with no new owner or fallback.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on `faeacc706b4887e65c4db1e6ac992179a6f82630`: the new case fails with the reported `FsSafeError`/`EEXIST` stack on Node and Bun. With this fix it passes, including actual Worker execution, recovery after removal of plugin files, canonical host state, and shared-file reads.
- The focused Bun file passes all 7 cases (6.02s wall, approximately 0.66s test time). Node passes the collision/Worker case and 4 other cases; the source-TS and compiled-CJS host-import cases fail identically on unchanged main. An explicit base replay produced those same two failures plus the new collision failure.
- All 26 direct/one-barrel consumer files were run on both runtimes: Node passed 470 tests with 1 existing skip and the 2 confirmed baseline failures (226.87s total); Bun passed 471 tests with 2 existing skips and no failures (258.82s total).
- `pnpm build` passed in 3m33s. Core TypeScript, plugin-test TypeScript, scoped oxlint/oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge passed (0 cycles). The full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted under the campaign's local gate budget.
- `package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --skip-build --runtime-only --allow-unreleased-changelog` produced an integrity-checked tarball. A fresh npm prefix and empty HOME/state were used, with approved package lifecycle scripts, a free loopback Gateway port, synthetic credentials, and a local Responses server. `openclaw.setup.activate` made **one actual HTTP request to the fixture**, with no creation collision. It then failed loading the missing declared `quickjs-wasi@3.6.2` dependency. A second empty-state run after installing that dependency in the disposable fixture again reached the provider, then failed with `Standalone plugin input contains a directory cycle`. Direct capture tracing confirms re-entry into the already-scanning OpenAI plugin directory. Neither run proves complete activation; both Gateways shut down cleanly. No operator state or real provider credentials were used.
- One consumer attempt was discarded because it overlapped packaging's temporary manifest rewrite. The reported consumer runs started only after packaging restored the source manifest.
- Independent Codex review reported no actionable P0–P2 findings in the supplied patch. The first attempt rejected shared temporary storage; a second attempt used the operating system's private temporary directory and passed the enforced isolation checks. The reviewer did not execute project code.

Reproduction/validation commands used isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under the lane's artifacts directory:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/plugin-bundled-reload.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/plugin-bundled-reload.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Both runtimes also received all 26 files found by:
rg -l 'plugin-generation-(capture|file-capture|artifact)' --glob '*.test.ts' src extensions packages test
pnpm tsgo:core
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json --incremental
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/plugins/plugin-generation-capture.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-file-capture.ts src/plugins/plugin-bundled-reload.test.ts
pnpm check:madge-import-cycles
pnpm build
```
